proposedClaim: The study indexes 925 distinct YouTube video IDs.
cannotEstablish: 925 is a curated union, not the number of all videos on these accounts or all ET-channeling videos.

proposedClaim: The index retains 256 account groups; 180 have linked video observations.
cannotEstablish: Account groups are not distinct human mediums. Unresolved aliases may remain separate.

proposedClaim: 881 indexed videos have usable durations: 877 current watch-page values and 4 inherited values.
cannotEstablish: A pooled all-source mean must not be labeled wholly independently verified.

proposedClaim: Per-account means and medians summarize available indexed uploads.
cannotEstablish: Recent-upload caps, mixed formats, selection and missingness prevent channel-wide estimation.

proposedClaim: 878 videos have current exact publication metadata;880 have retained exact dates overall.
cannotEstablish: Indexed month counts are not complete upload rates. UTC normalization can shift dates by one day. Upload date is not necessarily recording/session date; a recent repost does not establish that the featured practitioner is currently active.

proposedClaim: English title eligibility is 742 documents; 706 are attributed and embedded for channel comparisons.
cannotEstablish: These denominators must not be substituted for 925 or used to infer non-English topic absence.

proposedClaim: The caption acquisition pilot attempted 36 items and obtained 34; 30 English documents enter the analysis.
cannotEstablish: The pilot is purposive and small; 34 available does not mean 34 English analytical documents.

proposedClaim: The 30 English caption documents come from 17 uploader groups, 13 with two documents and 4 withone.
cannotEstablish: Only 13 groups qualify for comparisons requiring two documents; uploader identity is not speaker identity.

proposedClaim: 28 of 30 analyzed caption documents are marked automatically generated; 2 are marked nonautomatic.
cannotEstablish: No systematic word-error rate or independent transcription accuracy estimate was performed.

proposedClaim: The model uses a pinned all-MiniLM-L6-v2 representation with joint name-and-genre masking and stated sensitivities.
cannotEstablish: Use established embedding baseline; no demonstrated state-of-the-art claim for this domain.

proposedClaim: Joint removal of names and genre/packaging terms changes title-pair ranking correlation; repeated-title exclusion has less effect in this sample.
cannotEstablish: Names and genre terms were not separately ablated. The sensitivity is not proof that semantic distinctions are independent of publishing style.

proposedClaim: Twenty-five videos have eligible matched text; 22 videos from 11 publishers contribute to the 55-pair matched channel-matrix comparison.
cannotEstablish: A pair is not an independent observational unit; no causal or general population claim follows.

proposedClaim: Within-publisher caption pairs have a different median cosine from between-publisher pairs.
cannotEstablish: Shared documents create dependence. Do not claim significance, a validated classifier, plagiarism, or shared supernatural source.

proposedClaim: Current uploader metadata corrects a Brad Johnson interview to Multidimensional Soul.
cannotEstablish: Guest/subject identity and publisher account must remain separate.

proposedClaim: The computational results study publicly distributed discourse labeled as channeling.
cannotEstablish: They neither verify nor refute the claimed extraterrestrial origin of any communication.

proposedClaim: The work has internal AI-agent review and reproducible checks.
cannotEstablish: This is not journal peer review, editorial acceptance or independent external expert validation.
reviewCompletionBoundary: Phase1 rounds1–3 and manuscript rounds4–5 have actual reviews; manuscript round6 remains pending at this review.

proposedClaim: Chunk weighting changes two of 13 publisher nearest-neighbor labels while preserving a high global pair rank correlation in the same selected caption cohort.
cannotEstablish: No ground-truth thematic validation, new corpus, speaker segmentation or population inference. Input derivation cannot be replayed from text-free public artifacts alone.
